findings.evidence: scripts/lean_source.py:295 `if opener == "(" and colon is not None:` — only parenthesized groups are collected; docstring at 275-276 states the dot-notation rationale.
findings.fix: Return every binder group tagged with its binder kind (explicit/implicit/instance/strict-implicit) and move the explicit-only filter into `lint-dot-notation.py`; drop the receiver/dot-notation wording from the shared docstrings.
findings.issue: `variable_bindings` is placed in the generic parser but silently applies dot-notation policy: it keeps only `(`-binders, documented as "Implicit and instance-implicit variables are intentionally omitted because they cannot be dot-notation receivers" (272-277), and `VariableBinding` is documented "for receiver matching" (59-60). A later hygiene check calling this reusable API gets a policy-filtered subset of the section variables with no signal.

findings.evidence: scripts/lint-dot-notation.py:135-158 contains only regex/delimiter walking over `strip_comments_and_strings(text)` and `skip_balanced`, both now imported from `lean_source`; no dot-notation namespace or receiver logic appears in it.
findings.fix: Move `_include_commands` to `scripts/lean_source.py` as a public `include_commands` next to `variable_bindings`, and import it in the lint. `_expression_returns_sort`/`_declaration_returns_sort` (lines 179-188, 288-308) are likewise keyword/header-level syntax rather than dot-notation policy and belong with the parser.
findings.issue: `_include_commands` is pure Lean command syntax (parses `include`/`omit`, the `in` one-shot form, and bare names) with no dot-notation policy, and it is the direct companion of `variable_bindings`: any consumer of section variables needs include/omit to know which are in scope. Splitting the pair across modules forces the next consumer to reimplement it.

summary: The new shared module is in the right place and no import is unused or overbroad, but the parser/policy line is drawn in the wrong spot: dot-notation policy leaked into scripts/lean_source.py while a pure syntactic command parser stayed behind in the lint.
